newsitem.title: USA: Microprocessor sales to leap 32.9 pct in 1997-WSTS.
newsitem.headline: Microprocessor sales to leap 32.9 pct in 1997-WSTS.

text.p: Worldwide sales of microprocessors will jump 32.9 percent to $24.6 billion this year, helping drive a recovery in the overall chip industry as DRAM memory chips continue to decline, an industry group said.

Sales of dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, which tumbled 38.5 percent in 1996 to $25.1 billion, are expected to fall a further 20 percent in 1997 to $20.1 billion, according to a midyear World Semiconductor Trade Statistics forecast.
Microprocessor revenues in 1997 will for the first time exceed DRAM chip sales, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association, which released the data.

But the midyear forecast also forecasts DRAM revenues will rebound in 1998 to $27.1 billion, up 35 percent from a 1997 trough, and by 40.4 percent in 1999 and 32.8 percent in 2000, when they should hit $50.6 billion.
Microprocessors are expected to grow 26 percent in 1998, 21.2 percent in 1999 and 19.4 percent in 2000, when total world microprocessor sales are due to reach $44.9 billion.

Microprocesors currently account for 17.8 percent of all semiconductor sales, a percentage that should rise to 18.3 percent by 2000, while DRAMs represent a smaller portion due to price recession resulting from excess inventory.
In 1997, memory chips will reporesent 14.6 percent of the global chip makret, a percentage that should start to grow again in 1998 to reach 20.6 percent of global sales in 2000.

The overall metal oxide memory market, which includes DRAMs, fell 32.6 percent in 1996 and the WSTS forecast forecasts another 19.3 percent decline in 1997 to $29.4 billion, with sales rebounding to $63.6 billion in 2000.

Consumption in the year 2000 in the Americas is due to remain relatively stable at about one third of the world's chips, while the Japanese market is projected to decline to 21.5 percent from 23.9 percent this year and Europe to remain around 21 percent of the global semiconductor market.

But the Asia Pacific region is expected to grow to 24.3 percent from 21.9 percent currently, according to the WSTS, which is a grouping of about 70 chip manufacturers that prepares a twice-yearly global forecast and tracks monthly sales.
